steps.prompt: If your school building could talk, what would it complain about?

cards.title: Personification
cards.body: Personification gives an object, animal, place or idea a human action, feeling or voice: “The stairs groaned.” “The sun smiled.” It makes the world of your story feel alive.

cards.title: An object with a personality
cards.text: The old car coughed, wheezed, and finally gave up at the bottom of the hill.
cards.note: Coughing and wheezing make the car sound tired and ill, like an old person. You can feel how worn out it is.

cards.title: Choose the action, choose the mood
cards.showing: The wind shoved us down the street and slammed the gate behind us.
cards.note: Shoving and slamming make the wind a bully. “The wind tickled our ears” would make it playful.

cards.title: Human actions
cards.prompt: Tap the two human actions in this sentence.
cards.text: The kettle grumbled on the stove while the toaster waited patiently for its turn.

prompts: Which object did you bring to life, and what personality did you give it?
How did your choice of human actions set the mood?
